abstract: To investigate whether the myelodysplastic syndrome stem cell (MDS-SC) could predict relapse and survival after treatment in MDS patients with excess blasts (MDSEB), we prospectively enrolled 143 cases receiving allografting. The characteristics of CD34+ MDS subsets were evaluated using single-cell proteogenomic techniques. These cells were detected by multiparameter flow cytometry (MFC) pre- and post-transplantation. The phenotypically defined (PD) CD34+CD38-cocktail+ (CD56/CD22/CD11b/CD7/Tim-3/CLL-1) MDS-SCs exhibited greater stemness and quiescence than PD CD34+CD38-MDS-SCs with other immunophenotypes. A high level of pre-transplantation PD CD34+CD38-cocktail+MDS-SCs (≥0.1064%) independently predicted 3-year cumulative incidence of relapse (CIR, P < .001). No association of pre-transplantation traditional MFC-based MDS cells with relapse was observed. Patients with positive post-transplantation PD CD34+CD38-cocktail+MDSSCs (≥0.0081%) experienced a higher 3-year CIR (40.4% versus 6.5%, P < .001) and lower disease-free survival (DFS, 57.4% versus 85.1%, P < .001) than those negative cases. Multivariate analysis revealed that positive post-transplantation PD CD34+CD38-cocktail+MDS-SCs independently predicted CIR (P < .001) and DFS (P < .001). Patients with post-transplantation traditional MFC-MRD positivity also had a higher CIR (60.0% versus 12.8%, P < .001) and lower DFS (40.0% versus 80.2%, P < .001) than those negative cases. The MDS-SC-based assay has higher sensitivity and C-index for MRD detection than the traditional MFC method. Our data suggest the potential superiority of the PD MDS-SC-based assay over the traditional MFC method for outcome prediction in MDS-EB patients.
